proposals.title: Fix tsconfig.json's include path so the build gate actually runs
proposals.rationale: tsconfig.json already lives inside todo-app/; its include paths resolve relative to its own location, so "todo-app/src" means todo-app/todo-app/src, which doesn't exist. Changing it to "src" is the direct, checkable fix for the TS18003 failure hit in 10 of 11 sessions. Directly verifiable by re-running `npm run build` after the change.

proposals.title: Pick one formatting enforcement mechanism

options.label: A: Adopt a formatter
options.change: Approve adding prettier as a dev dependency (the exact thing rejected mid-session in b6205fd8), add a `format` script, and rewrite the style guidance in CLAUDE.md/AGENT.md/style-consistency to point at it instead of 'match the surrounding file'.
options.tradeoffs: Removes the judgment call entirely — style stops being something an agent or human can get wrong. Costs a new dependency and a small amount of build-tooling churn, which is why this needs a human sign-off rather than a silent proposal.

options.label: B: Codify one explicit rule, no new dependency
options.change: Replace 'match the surrounding file's conventions' in both CLAUDE.md and AGENT.md with one explicit, stated rule (e.g. 'always single quotes'), and update style-consistency's SKILL.md to reference the same rule.
options.tradeoffs: Zero new dependencies or tooling. But it depends on every future session actually reading and following the text rule — it doesn't structurally prevent drift the way a formatter does, and f95c8207/b6205fd8 already show this codebase's style drifting twice under text-only guidance.

proposals.rationale: The diagnosis (three guides disagree, one confirmed regression) is solid, but which mechanism to adopt is a call about dependencies and enforcement style this data doesn't settle on its own.

proposals.title: Resolve the commit and plan-approval contradiction between CLAUDE.md and AGENT.md

options.label: A: AGENT.md wins on autonomy
options.change: Delete CLAUDE.md's 'commit once a piece of work is in a reasonable state' and 'run with it rather than stopping to wait for a go-ahead' lines. Agent never auto-commits, always stops after a plan for explicit approval.
options.tradeoffs: Matches what actually happened in e6041b83 — a human had to reject an autonomous commit the agent made following CLAUDE.md's wording. Slower iteration, more stop-and-wait turns.

options.label: B: CLAUDE.md wins on autonomy
options.change: Delete AGENT.md's 'do not commit changes automatically' and 'wait for them to say go' lines. Agent commits as work reaches a reasonable state and runs with plans without waiting.
options.tradeoffs: Faster iteration, fewer interruptions. But the only real evidence in this dataset (e6041b83) is a human actively blocking exactly this behavior — this option runs against the one data point available, not with it.

proposals.rationale: Both files are internally consistent on their own; the conflict is between them, and nothing in harness-snapshot.json or index.json states which one the team actually wants. This is a values call, not a bug.

proposals.title: Fix the broken SKILLS.md reference
proposals.diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/todo-app/SKILLS.md
@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+# Skills
+
+- **code-formatter** — Use for formatting and style nits in this repo — spacing, quote style, import order, small naming tweaks. Scope is src/.
+- **plan-and-ship** — Use when someone asks for a plan, approach, or design for a change in this repo.
+- **refactor-cleanup** — For when a piece of code has grown messy and needs a proper cleanup pass — extra abstraction, duplicated logic, confusing structure. Most relevant in src/state, src/features, and src/components.
+- **style-consistency** — The codebase mixes naming conventions and folder depth across files (camelCase, kebab-case, PascalCase, inconsistent nesting). Use this to bring a file or folder in line with the convention used elsewhere.
proposals.rationale: Every name and summary here is already present in harness-snapshot.json's `skills` array — nothing about this fix requires inventing content or making a judgment call, only assembling what's already there. Alternative mechanical option: delete the two references to SKILLS.md in CLAUDE.md instead, if the team would rather not maintain a second skill index.

proposals.title: Remove or revive the two hooks unrelated to the commit-policy question
proposals.rationale: Both hooks are loc_active: 0 while registered live — a verifiable fact, not a judgment call. Defaulting to removing the dead registration (rather than restoring hook bodies neither this analysis nor the transcripts specify) is the safer of the two mechanical options and doesn't touch the still-open commit-policy question. If the team would rather revive these two instead of removing them, that's an equally mechanical alternative — pick either, just don't leave the registration lying to settings.json readers.

proposals.title: post-edit-autocommit.js: do not propose a fix yet
proposals.rationale: This hook's entire purpose — maintaining a running auto-commit trail — is the exact behavior AGENT.md forbids and CLAUDE.md invites, i.e. proposal #3. Reviving it presumes option B there; deleting its registration presumes option A. Proposing either now would silently decide proposal #3 on the team's behalf. Wait for #3 to resolve, then this becomes mechanical.

proposals.title: Determine the team's actual target shell/OS before writing anything into the guides
proposals.harness_component: todo-app/CLAUDE.md and todo-app/AGENT.md (neither states an OS/shell)
proposals.next_step: Ask the team, or check for an authoritative source outside these three files (CI config, a devcontainer/.tool-versions file, package.json engines/os fields) — don't infer an answer from these transcripts. The transcripts themselves are inconsistent: 7c3e9b15/b6205fd8/48a7d3c1 show a Unix `head` call failing with a PowerShell-style error, and in 48a7d3c1 the very next attempt (`Get-Content`, real PowerShell syntax) fails too, this time with a bash-style error. That's contradictory evidence about which shell is actually in play — writing a guessed answer into CLAUDE.md would just replace one wrong assumption (the agent's) with another (this skill's).
